Examples: "News Org A noBylinesPolicy 'https://news.example.com/bylines'", "Journalism Company B noBylinesPolicy 'Our policy is to omit bylines for staff editorials.'", "Media Outlet C noBylinesPolicy 'https://media.example.org/editorial-standards#bylines'".

candidates.label: creator
candidates.comment: An authorship relation between a creative work or user comment and the person or organization responsible for its creation. Also called: author, originator, producer, made by. Examples: "Novel" creator "Jane Doe", "Software" creator "Acme Corp.", "Blog Post" creator "John Smith", "User Review" creator "Anonymous User". Distinct from copyrightHolder, which is about legal ownership.

candidates.label: manufacturer
candidates.comment: A manufacturing relation between a product and the organization that produced it. Also called: produced by, made by, fabricated by. Examples: "Smartphone manufacturer Apple", "Automobile manufacturer Toyota", "Furniture manufacturer IKEA".

candidates.label: correctionsPolicy
candidates.comment: A policy relation between an organization and the statement describing its disclosure and correction policy for errors. Also called: error policy, editorial policy, disclosure policy. Examples: "The New York Times" corrections policy "Our commitment to accuracy and transparency...", "Example Corp." corrections policy "Policy on correcting factual errors.", "Academic Journal" corrections policy "Guidelines for authors on submitting corrections.".

candidates.label: legislationPassedBy
candidates.comment: A passing authority relation between a piece of legislation and the organization or person that originally enacted it. Also called: enacted by, made by, legislated by. Examples: "Primary Legislation legislationPassedBy Parliament", "Secondary Legislation legislationPassedBy Government", "Local Bylaw legislationPassedBy City Council". Distinct from legislationResponsible, which refers to the ministry or individual in charge of elaborating or addressing questions about the legislation.

candidates.label: discusses
candidates.comment: A discussion relation between a user comment and the creative work it is associated with. Also called "comments on", "pertains to", "about". Examples: "User comment 'Great movie!' discusses 'The Matrix'", "Blog post comment discusses 'Article on AI'", "Review discusses 'New Album by Artist X'". Distinct from discussionUrl, which is a link to the page containing comments about a creative work.

candidates.label: spokenByCharacter
candidates.comment: An attribution relation between a quotation and the character, person, or organization to whom it is attributed within a creative work. Also called "attributed to", "quote speaker", "character says", "uttered by". Examples: "The quote is spokenByCharacter Hamlet", "The dialogue was spokenByCharacter the CEO", "This line is spokenByCharacter a fictional narrator."

chosen_property.label: winner
chosen_property.justification: Inverse of winner property fits the relation phrase and instances.

candidates.label: winner
candidates.comment: A winner relation between a losing action and the person who won it. Also called victor, triumphant participant, successful party. Examples: ChessMatchLoseAction winner Alice, RaceLoseAction winner Bob, CompetitionLoseAction winner Charlie.

candidates.label: loser
candidates.comment: A losing participant relation between a win action and the person who lost. Also called: defeated participant, vanquished, runner-up. Examples: "Chess Match WinAction loser Opponent B", "Race WinAction loser Second Place Runner", "Debate WinAction loser Team B".

candidates.label: opponent
candidates.comment: A person who is an opponent in an exercise action. Also called adversary, competitor, rival. Examples: "Boxing Match opponent 'Mike Tyson'", "Chess Game opponent 'Deep Blue'", "Tennis Match opponent 'Serena Williams'". Distinct from participant, which is a general participant.

candidates.label: award
candidates.comment: An award won by or for a creative work, organization, person, product, or service. Also called: honor, prize, recognition. Examples: "CreativeWork 'Movie' award 'Oscar'", "Organization 'Company X' award 'Best Employer'", "Person 'Scientist' award 'Nobel Prize'". Distinct from awards, which is the plural form.

candidates.label: awards
candidates.comment: Awards won by or for a creative work, organization, person, or product. Also called: honors, prizes, recognitions. Examples: "CreativeWork 'Movie' awards 'Oscar'", "Organization 'Company X' awards 'Best Employer'", "Person 'Scientist' awards 'Nobel Prize'". Distinct from award, which is the singular form.

candidates.label: competitor
candidates.comment: A participation relation in a sports event, indicating a person or sports team that is competing. Also called "participant", "opponent", "rival". Examples: "Olympic race sports event competitor Usain Bolt", "Football match sports event competitor Manchester United".

candidates.label: awayTeam
candidates.comment: A person or sports team designated as the away team in a sports event. Also called: visiting team, opponent. Examples: "SportsEvent 'Football Match' awayTeam 'Team B'", "SportsEvent 'Basketball Game' awayTeam 'Lakers'". Distinct from homeTeam, which is the team playing at their home venue.

candidates.label: antagonist
candidates.comment: An antagonist relation between a muscle and another muscle whose action opposes it. Also called opposing muscle, counteracting muscle. Examples: "The biceps' antagonist is the 'triceps'.", "The quadriceps' antagonist is the 'hamstrings'."

candidates.label: candidate
candidates.comment: A participation relation in a vote action, indicating the person who is being voted for. Also called "voted for", "nominee", "electoral candidate". Examples: "Election vote action candidate Jane Smith", "Award vote action candidate John Doe".

candidates.label: game
candidates.comment: A game relation between a game server and the video game that is hosted and played on it. Also called: hosted game, server game, game played. Examples: "Minecraft Server" game "Minecraft", "World of Warcraft Realm" game "World of Warcraft", "CS:GO Server" game "Counter-Strike: Global Offensive".

chosen_property.label: winner
chosen_property.justification: Inverse of winner property fits the relation phrase and instances.

candidates.label: winner
candidates.comment: A winner relation between a losing action and the person who won it. Also called victor, triumphant participant, successful party. Examples: ChessMatchLoseAction winner Alice, RaceLoseAction winner Bob, CompetitionLoseAction winner Charlie.

candidates.label: loser
candidates.comment: A losing participant relation between a win action and the person who lost. Also called: defeated participant, vanquished, runner-up. Examples: "Chess Match WinAction loser Opponent B", "Race WinAction loser Second Place Runner", "Debate WinAction loser Team B".

candidates.label: tracks
candidates.comment: A tracks relation between a music group or playlist and a music recording, typically a single song. Also called song, musical piece, recording. Examples: "MusicPlaylist tracks 'Bohemian Rhapsody'", "MusicGroup tracks 'Stairway to Heaven'", "Album tracks 'Track 3'". Distinct from track, which can also refer to an ItemList of music recordings.

candidates.label: track
candidates.comment: A track relation between a music group or playlist and a music recording, typically a single song. Also called song, musical piece, recording. Examples: "MusicPlaylist track 'Bohemian Rhapsody'", "MusicGroup track 'Stairway to Heaven'", "Album track 'Track 3'". Distinct from tracks, which is a more general property for multiple music recordings.

candidates.label: opponent
candidates.comment: A person who is an opponent in an exercise action. Also called adversary, competitor, rival. Examples: "Boxing Match opponent 'Mike Tyson'", "Chess Game opponent 'Deep Blue'", "Tennis Match opponent 'Serena Williams'". Distinct from participant, which is a general participant.

candidates.label: recordingOf
candidates.comment: A recording of relation between a music recording and the music composition it represents. Also called rendition of, version of, based on composition. Examples: "A music recording 'Bohemian Rhapsody' is a recording of 'the Queen composition'.", "A classical track is a recording of 'Beethoven's Symphony No. 9'.", "A cover song is a recording of 'the original composition'.". Distinct from recordedAs, which is the inverse relation.

candidates.label: numTracks
candidates.comment: The total number of tracks contained within a music playlist or album. Also called track count, song count, number of songs. Examples: "Album X numTracks 12", "Playlist Y numTracks 50", "EP Z numTracks 4". Distinct from numberOfEpisodes, which is for seasons or series.

candidates.label: recordedAs
candidates.comment: A recording relation between a music composition and an audio recording of that work. Also called recorded version, audio rendition. Examples: "A music composition 'Symphony No. 5' is recorded as 'Berlin Philharmonic recording'.", "A song 'Yesterday' is recorded as 'The Beatles' original recording'.", "A classical piece is recorded as 'a live performance album'.". Distinct from recordingOf, which is the inverse relation.

candidates.label: musicalKey
candidates.comment: The key, mode, or scale used in a music composition. Also called key signature, composition key, tonal center. Examples: "Symphony No. 5 musicalKey 'C minor'", "Für Elise musicalKey 'A minor'", "Jazz Standard musicalKey 'Bb Major'".

candidates.label: byArtist
candidates.comment: A performance relation between a music album or recording and the music group or person who performed it. Also called "performed by", "artist of", "featuring artist". Examples: "Album 'Thriller' byArtist Michael Jackson", "Recording 'Bohemian Rhapsody' byArtist Queen". Distinct from composer, which is the person who wrote the music, whereas byArtist is the performer.

chosen_property.label: about
chosen_property.justification: Inverse of about property fits the relation phrase and instances.

candidates.label: lyricist
candidates.comment: A lyricist relation between a music composition and the person who wrote its words. Also called: songwriter, words by, author of lyrics. Examples: "Bohemian Rhapsody lyricist Freddie Mercury", "Yesterday lyricist Paul McCartney", "Hallelujah lyricist Leonard Cohen".

candidates.label: composer
candidates.comment: A creative role relation between an event or music composition and the organization or person who wrote it. Also called "writer", "creator", "author of music". Examples: "Symphony music composition composer Ludwig van Beethoven", "Concert event composer Wolfgang Amadeus Mozart". Distinct from byArtist, which is the performer of a musical work.

candidates.label: author
candidates.comment: An organization or person who created content or a rating. Also called: creator, writer, originator, composer. Examples: "CreativeWork 'Novel' author 'Jane Austen'", "Rating 'Product Review' author 'Consumer Reports'", "CreativeWork 'Article' author 'New York Times'". Distinct from artist, which is typically for visual or comic art.

candidates.label: about
candidates.comment: A subject matter relation between an entity (e.g., a creative work, event, or communication) and the topic it concerns. Also called concerning, regarding, on the topic of, related to. Examples: "A book about quantum physics.", "A lecture about climate change.", "A certification about data privacy."

candidates.label: language
candidates.comment: A communication medium relation between a communicate action or write action and the language employed in that action. Also called language used, medium of communication, spoken in, written in. Examples: A communicate action uses the language 'English'. A write action uses the language 'French'. A conversation has the language 'Spanish'. Distinct from inLanguage, which is for the language of a creative work itself, not the action of communicating/writing.

candidates.label: mentions
candidates.comment: A mention relation between a creative work and a thing it references without necessarily being about. Also called: references, alludes to, cites. Examples: "News Article mentions 'Climate Change'", "Book mentions 'Historical Event'", "Speech mentions 'Famous Person'". Distinct from about, which indicates the primary topic of the creative work.

candidates.label: creator
candidates.comment: An authorship relation between a creative work or user comment and the person or organization responsible for its creation. Also called: author, originator, producer, made by. Examples: "Novel" creator "Jane Doe", "Software" creator "Acme Corp.", "Blog Post" creator "John Smith", "User Review" creator "Anonymous User". Distinct from copyrightHolder, which is about legal ownership.

candidates.label: discusses
candidates.comment: A discussion relation between a user comment and the creative work it is associated with. Also called "comments on", "pertains to", "about". Examples: "User comment 'Great movie!' discusses 'The Matrix'", "Blog post comment discusses 'Article on AI'", "Review discusses 'New Album by Artist X'". Distinct from discussionUrl, which is a link to the page containing comments about a creative work.

candidates.label: editor
candidates.comment: An editor relation between a creative work and the person who edited it. Also called "edited by", "compiled by", "prepared by". Examples: "Book 'The Great Gatsby' editor 'Maxwell Perkins'", "Journal article editor 'Dr. Jane Doe'", "Film 'Pulp Fiction' editor 'Sally Menke'".

candidates.label: publishedBy
candidates.comment: A publisher relation between a publication event and the organization or person responsible for it. Also called published by, issued by, released by. Examples: "A book's publication event was published by 'Penguin Random House'.", "A journal article's publication event was published by 'Elsevier'.", "A blog post's publication event was published by 'Jane Doe'.". Distinct from publisher, which refers to the publisher of the creative work itself.

chosen_property.label: reportedOn
chosen_property.definition: Reported on a person or event
chosen_property.justification: No existing property fits the relation phrase and instances.

candidates.label: reportNumber
candidates.comment: A report number relation between a report and the unique identifier assigned by its publisher. Also called report ID, document number. Examples: "A financial report has a report number 'FY2023-Q4'.", "A technical report has a report number 'TR-001-2024'.", "A government report has a report number 'GAO-24-123'."

candidates.label: dateline
candidates.comment: A textual origin relation between a news article and the brief text describing where and when the story was written or filed. Also called: news origin, article origin, reporting location. Examples: "News Report" dateline "BEIRUT, Lebanon, June 2.", "Article" dateline "Paris, France", "Dispatch" dateline "December 19, 2017 11:43AM Reporting from Washington". Distinct from locationCreated, which is a structured representation of the creation location.

candidates.label: knownVehicleDamages
candidates.comment: A vehicle condition relation between a vehicle and a textual description of its known damages, whether repaired or not. Also called vehicle damage report, damage history, known defects, condition notes. Examples: A used car has knownVehicleDamages 'minor dent on rear bumper'. A vehicle has knownVehicleDamages 'repaired fender bender'. A truck has knownVehicleDamages 'scratches on passenger side door'. Distinct from vehicleCondition, which is a general assessment, not specific damages.

candidates.label: healthcareReportingData
candidates.comment: A healthcare reporting data relation between a hospital and its associated reporting data, such as CDC records or datasets. Also called hospital data, reporting dataset, healthcare metrics. Examples: "A hospital has healthcare reporting data from the CDC.", "The hospital provides healthcare reporting data as a dataset.", "This facility publishes its healthcare reporting data."

candidates.label: diversityStaffingReport
candidates.comment: A diversity staffing report relation between an organization (e.g., news media) and an article or URL containing a report on staffing diversity issues. Also called "staff diversity report", "workforce diversity data", "inclusion metrics report". Examples: "News media organization diversityStaffingReport 'Article on newsroom diversity'", "Company diversityStaffingReport 'URL to annual diversity report'", "Organization diversityStaffingReport 'Self-reported staffing data'".

candidates.label: isLiveBroadcast
candidates.comment: A broadcast status relation indicating whether a broadcast event is being transmitted in real-time. Also called live stream, real-time broadcast, live transmission. Examples: A sports game broadcast has isLiveBroadcast set to 'true'. A news report broadcast has isLiveBroadcast set to 'true'. A recorded TV show broadcast has isLiveBroadcast set to 'false'.

candidates.label: publishedOn
candidates.comment: A broadcast publication relation between a publication event and the broadcast service on which it was published. Also called aired on, broadcast via, released on service. Examples: "A TV show's publication event was published on 'BBC One'.", "A radio program's publication event was published on 'NPR'.", "A news segment's publication event was published on 'CNN'."

candidates.label: coverageEndTime
candidates.comment: A temporal boundary relation between a live blog posting and the time when its event coverage concludes. Also called: coverage end, reporting end time, live blog conclusion. Examples: "Election Night Live Blog" coverage end time "2024-11-06T04:00:00Z", "Sports Event Live Update" coverage end time "2023-07-15T19:30:00Z", "Conference Live Blog" coverage end time "2023-10-27T17:00:00Z". Distinct from coverageStartTime, which indicates when coverage begins.

candidates.label: recordedIn
candidates.comment: A recording capture relation between an event and the creative work that captured all or part of it. Also called captured by, documented in, featured in. Examples: "A concert event was recorded in 'a live album'.", "A historical event was recorded in 'a documentary film'.", "A speech event was recorded in 'a news broadcast'.". Distinct from recordedAt, which is the inverse relation.

candidates.label: coverageStartTime
candidates.comment: A temporal boundary relation between a live blog posting and the time when its event coverage begins. Also called: coverage start, reporting start time, live blog commencement. Examples: "Election Night Live Blog" coverage start time "2024-11-05T18:00:00Z", "Sports Event Live Update" coverage start time "2023-07-15T14:00:00Z", "Conference Live Blog" coverage start time "2023-10-27T09:00:00Z". Distinct from coverageEndTime, which indicates when coverage concludes.

chosen_property.label: announced
chosen_property.justification: No existing property fits the relation phrase and instances.

candidates.label: announcementLocation
candidates.comment: An announcement location relation between a special announcement and the specific civic structure or local business it pertains to. Also called relevant location, associated place, specific venue. Examples: "A special announcement's announcement location is 'City Hall'.", "The emergency announcement's announcement location is 'Local Grocery Store'." Distinct from spatialCoverage, which is used for larger geographic regions.

candidates.label: diseasePreventionInfo
candidates.comment: A disease prevention information relation between a special announcement and a URL or web content providing details about disease prevention. Also called "prevention guidelines", "health advice". Examples: "Special announcement diseasePreventionInfo 'cdc.gov/prevention'", "Public health alert diseasePreventionInfo 'WebContent on handwashing'", "COVID-19 update diseasePreventionInfo 'who.int/prevention'".

candidates.label: newsUpdatesAndGuidelines
candidates.comment: A URL or web content providing news updates and guidelines related to a special announcement. Also called updates page, guidelines link, news and guidance. Examples: "COVID-19 Announcement newsUpdatesAndGuidelines 'https://example.com/covid-updates'", "Emergency Alert newsUpdatesAndGuidelines 'https://gov.example.org/emergency-guidelines'", "Product Recall newsUpdatesAndGuidelines 'https://company.com/recall-info'".

candidates.label: gettingTestedInfo
candidates.comment: A getting tested info relation between a special announcement and information regarding testing for a medical condition. Also called: testing information, diagnostic details, screening guidance. Examples: "COVID-19 Announcement" getting tested info "CDC Testing Guidelines", "Flu Season Alert" getting tested info "Local Clinic Testing Sites", "Public Health Notice" getting tested info "Symptoms and Testing Advice".

candidates.label: publicTransportClosuresInfo
candidates.comment: A public transport closures information relation between a special announcement and details regarding public transport disruptions. Also called transport closure details, public transit alerts. Examples: "A special announcement includes public transport closures info about subway lines.", "An emergency alert provides public transport closures info for bus routes.", "A news update contains public transport closures info for train services."

candidates.label: schoolClosuresInfo
candidates.comment: Information regarding school closures, typically provided as a URL or web content within a special announcement. Also called school closing details, closure announcement, education disruption info. Examples: `Emergency Announcement` schoolClosuresInfo `URL to district website`, `Weather Alert` schoolClosuresInfo `Text about snow day`, `Public Health Notice` schoolClosuresInfo `WebContent on school status`.

candidates.label: datePosted
candidates.comment: A temporal publication relation between a CDCPMD record, job posting, real estate listing, or special announcement and its online publication date. Also called: posting date, publication date, listing date. Examples: "Job Opening" date posted "2023-10-25", "Apartment for Rent" date posted "2023-10-20", "Public Health Alert" date posted "2023-03-01T09:00:00Z". Distinct from datePublished, which is a more general property for first publication.

candidates.label: releasedEvent
candidates.comment: A released event relation between a creative work and the publication event marking its release. Also called release event, launch event. Examples: "A movie has a released event 'Premiere at Cannes Film Festival'.", "A book has a released event 'Book Launch Party'.", "A video game has a released event 'E3 Announcement'."

candidates.label: acceptedOffer
candidates.comment: An accepted offer relation between an order and the specific offer(s) that were agreed upon and included in it. Also called purchased offer, confirmed offer, included offer. Examples: "A customer's order accepted an offer for a laptop.", "The order accepted an offer for two books."

candidates.label: releaseDate
candidates.comment: A release date relation between a product and the date it was made available to the public. Also called launch date, availability date, publication date. Examples: "A new smartphone model has a release date of 2024-03-01.", "A software update has a release date of 2023-11-15.", "A new car model has a release date of 2025-01-01.". Distinct from productionDate, which is when the item was manufactured.

chosen_property.label: broadcastOfEvent
chosen_property.justification: Inverse of broadcastOfEvent property fits the relation phrase and instances.

candidates.label: broadcastOfEvent
candidates.comment: An event that is being broadcast by a broadcast event. Also called: televised event, event broadcast. Examples: "BroadcastEvent 'Super Bowl Live' broadcastOfEvent 'Super Bowl LVIII'", "BroadcastEvent 'Concert Stream' broadcastOfEvent 'Live Music Concert'."

candidates.label: broadcaster
candidates.comment: An ownership or operational relation between a broadcast service and the organization responsible for it. Also called "service provider", "operated by", "owned by", "broadcast by". Examples: "BBC Radio 4 broadcaster BBC", "CNN broadcast service broadcaster Warner Bros. Discovery".

candidates.label: broadcastAffiliateOf
candidates.comment: An organization representing the media network(s) whose content is broadcast on a broadcast service. Also called: network affiliation, broadcast network. Examples: "BroadcastService 'Local TV Station' broadcastAffiliateOf 'NBC'", "BroadcastService 'Radio Station' broadcastAffiliateOf 'NPR'."

candidates.label: broadcastFrequency
candidates.comment: A frequency used for over-the-air broadcasts for a broadcast channel or service. Also called: broadcast frequency, radio frequency, channel frequency. Examples: "BroadcastChannel 'FM Station' broadcastFrequency '87.9 FM'", "BroadcastService 'TV Channel' broadcastFrequency 'BroadcastFrequencySpecification 500 MHz'."

candidates.label: broadcastChannelId
candidates.comment: A unique address by which a broadcast service can be identified in a provider lineup. Also called: channel number, broadcast ID, station ID. Examples: "BroadcastChannel 'Channel 7' broadcastChannelId '7'", "BroadcastChannel 'ESPN' broadcastChannelId '206'."

candidates.label: isLiveBroadcast
candidates.comment: A broadcast status relation indicating whether a broadcast event is being transmitted in real-time. Also called live stream, real-time broadcast, live transmission. Examples: A sports game broadcast has isLiveBroadcast set to 'true'. A news report broadcast has isLiveBroadcast set to 'true'. A recorded TV show broadcast has isLiveBroadcast set to 'false'.

candidates.label: broadcastSubChannel
candidates.comment: A subchannel identification for a broadcast frequency specification. Also called "subchannel of broadcast", "broadcast channel identifier". Examples: "FM 98.1 specification broadcastSubChannel 'HD2'", "Digital TV channel 5 specification broadcastSubChannel '5.3'".

candidates.label: broadcastDisplayName
candidates.comment: A name displayed in the channel guide for a broadcast service. Also called: channel name, station display name. Examples: "BroadcastService 'Local News' broadcastDisplayName 'WXYZ-TV'", "BroadcastService 'Music Radio' broadcastDisplayName 'KEXP 90.3 FM'."

candidates.label: broadcastFrequencyValue
candidates.comment: A number or quantitative value representing the frequency in MHz for a particular broadcast. Also called: frequency in MHz, broadcast megahertz. Examples: "BroadcastFrequencySpecification 'FM 98.1' broadcastFrequencyValue '98.1'", "BroadcastFrequencySpecification 'TV Channel 25' broadcastFrequencyValue '539'."

candidates.label: broadcastServiceTier
candidates.comment: A textual description of the type of service required to access a broadcast channel. Also called: channel tier, service level, subscription tier. Examples: "BroadcastChannel 'Premium Movies' broadcastServiceTier 'Premium'", "BroadcastChannel 'Basic News' broadcastServiceTier 'Standard'."
